prompt.context: Our client, a US based e-commerce company, ShopOn, has seen a rise in customer returns over the last few quarters. Even though its revenue and market share have been increasing every quarter, the CEO is concerned that customer returns will start impacting the margins soon.
prompt.question: The CEO of ShopOn wants your help to identify the reasons behind the high rate of returns and create a mitigation strategy.

clarifying_info.q: What counts as a customer return?
clarifying_info.a: Customer returns refer to products returned by customers post-delivery and not order cancellations before delivery.
The return period for any ShopOn product is 30 days from the day of delivery.

Even though new competitors keep entering the market, there has been no new competitor in the last few quarters that could bring about any significant change to ShopOn. ShopOn is ranked #3 in the e-commerce space.

clarifying_info.q: How does ShopOn's inventory model work?
clarifying_info.a: ShopOn holds 50% of the product inventory in its warehouses and 50% is a marketplace for sellers.

clarifying_info.q: What time horizon should the mitigation strategy cover?
clarifying_info.a: The mitigation strategy should focus on both short-term (next 1-3 quarters) and long-term action items (next 2-3 years).

clarifying_info.q: Is there a budget or investment guidance?
clarifying_info.a: No investment guidance has been provided.

exhibits.title: Product Mix and Returns Rate by Category
exhibits.shows: Two pie charts showing % of units sold by product category in Q1 and Q2, alongside a table of returns % by product category.

framework: 1. Change in product mix — has the share of high-return categories (Apparel, Household) grown?
2. Product issues — size/fit/color for Apparel; damaged/malfunctioning for Electronics; damaged/color/size for Household; expired/seal broken for Food
3. Pricing issues — better price available elsewhere or now available cheaper on ShopOn itself
4. Delivery issues — product arrived late, wrong product delivered, shipping box damaged
5. Other reasons — inaccurate website description, no longer needed, bought by mistake, previously out-of-stock item now back, fraudulent behavior (used then returned within policy)

questions.prompt: Using the exhibits, calculate ShopOn's overall customer returns % in Q1 and Q2, and explain what drove the change.
questions.guidance: Candidate should weight each category's return % by its share of units sold and sum to get the blended rate. The key insight is that the mix shifted toward higher-return categories (Apparel rose from 15% to 30%, Household from 15% to 20%) while lower-return Electronics fell from 35% to 25%, driving the total return rate up.

math.setup: Blended return % = sum of (% units sold in category × category return %). Calculate for Q1 and Q2 separately.
math.answer: Q1 blended return rate = 3.00%; Q2 blended return rate = 3.45%. The 0.45 pp increase is driven by a product mix shift: Apparel (highest return rate at 5%) grew from 15% to 30% of units sold, and Household (4%) grew from 15% to 20%, while Electronics (lowest at 2%) shrank from 35% to 25%.

brainstorming.prompt: We now know that the apparel business is leading to increased returns. Further analysis reveals a large number of apparel products had quality issues and were being returned. What are the various costs involved with a return in the apparel business, and how can we reduce those costs?

categories.name: Costs — Return without replacement
ideas: Re-packaging cost if product is not damaged
Shipping cost to seller if product is damaged

categories.name: Costs — Return with replacement product
ideas: Product cost if original product not returned
Shipping cost to seller if original product is damaged

categories.name: Ways to reduce costs
ideas: Ask customer to re-package the item before returning the order
Provide customer with the seller's address to ship returns directly, bypassing ShopOn warehouse
Charge customer if original product is not returned within 30 days
Renegotiate supplier contracts so suppliers bear COGS in case of quality-related returns
Improve warehouse processes to ensure correct orders are sent, reducing erroneous shipments

recommendation: Reduce the returns % of the apparel business by delisting products with poor ratings
Reduce apparel return rate by onboarding verified sellers and blacklisting sellers with poor reviews
Reduce return costs by requiring customers to inspect the product at the time of delivery
risks: ShopOn could lose market share to a competitor, especially in the apparel business, if return policies become stricter
ShopOn might become unpopular among sellers if they are penalized or blacklisted
Customers may not be available or comfortable opening products at time of delivery
next_steps: Conduct cost-benefit analysis of penalizing customers and suppliers for quality-related returns
Review competition's seller agreements to avoid being the less attractive platform for sellers
Modify product specifications and descriptions on the website for items with recurring return issues
Establish a feedback and blacklisting process for sellers with recurring quality issues
Build an automated system to alert both ShopOn and sellers when a product rating falls below a defined threshold
